articles.title: HOW INTENT-BASED, PRIVILEGED ACCESS CONTROLS SECURE AI AGENTS
articles.summary:
What makes AI agents so powerful is also what makes them a liability: they can act autonomously at machine speed. If they have broad access permissions, they can overreach even when performing seemingly minor tasks.

In Securing the Agentic Enterprise [5], you'll learn:

* How to identify risks of inherited credentials, standing access, and unpredictable agent behavior * How intent-based, just-in-time, and just-enough access limits agentic risk * How 1Password Privileged Access extends access governance to AI agents and other non-human identities

articles.title: OUTLOOK.COM BOUNCES LEGIT EMAILS AS MICROSOFT'S AUTHENTICATION CRACKDOWN GOES SIDEWAYS
articles.summary: Microsoft's consumer email services are rejecting legitimate messages following changes to sender authentication enforcement. Users report SPF and DMARC validation failures, including some from apparently compliant domains. A Microsoft support moderator acknowledged a service degradation, leaving administrators and senders dealing with intermittent delivery failures.

articles.title: GOOGLE UNVEILS NEW AI CHIP VARIANTS AS CLOUD DEMAND SURGES
articles.summary: Google introduced two specialized TPU variants to challenge Nvidia and expand its cloud AI infrastructure business. The 8tx combines Google silicon with AMD processors and hardware-level encryption for sensitive workloads, while the 8i Max delivers additional memory and compute capacity for demanding reasoning, coding, and scientific applications.

articles.title: MEMORY CRUNCH MAKES REFURBISHED KIT LOOK A LOT LESS SECONDHAND
articles.summary: Surging memory prices are making refurbished PCs and enterprise hardware increasingly attractive. Suppliers report growing interest in extending device lifecycles, trade-in programs, and refurbished equipment backed by warranties of up to three years. Rising component costs and tighter IT budgets are pushing organizations to reconsider traditional hardware refresh cycles.

articles.title: ENTERPRISES PREP FOR INFLUX OF PERSONAL AI AGENTS
articles.summary: Enterprises are preparing for growing traffic from personal AI agents such as Meta's Muse and Instinct, viewing them as potential sales channels and governance challenges. Companies including Shopify, Hilton, and Rocket are adapting their platforms and APIs to support AI-driven transactions. While traffic remains relatively small, executives are increasingly focused on authentication, regulatory compliance, and preserving direct customer relationships.

articles.title: THE CIO JOB DESCRIPTION IS BEING REWRITTEN IN REAL TIME
articles.summary: The CIO role is shifting from managing technology delivery toward redesigning business processes and demonstrating measurable outcomes. Technology leaders increasingly face questions about productivity, organizational change, and accountability for AI-driven decisions. Traditional measures such as uptime, project completion, and system reliability remain essential but are no longer sufficient.

articles.title: WHY THE CYBERPOCALYPSE MIGHT HIT CHINA HARDER
articles.summary: AI-driven vulnerability discovery is accelerating the race between finding and patching software flaws. China's state-directed cybersecurity strategy and restrictions on vulnerability disclosure could leave its systems at a disadvantage compared with more open disclosure ecosystems. As AI makes previously scarce vulnerabilities easier to discover, rapid remediation may become increasingly important.

articles.title: NEW RESEARCH: VIRTUAL MACHINES REMAIN CENTRAL TO CLOUD NATIVE INFRASTRUCTURE AS AI WORKLOADS EVOLVE
articles.summary: A Linux Foundation study sponsored by CNCF and Broadcom, covering 492 practitioners, found that virtual machines account for an average of 53% of production applications. Most respondents expect their VM footprint to remain relatively stable as Kubernetes adoption grows. The findings suggest enterprises will continue operating mixed VM and container environments, particularly as AI workloads introduce new isolation requirements.

articles.title: IMAGINE THE DAY WHEN YOUR DATA CAN PROTECT ITSELF. THAT DAY IS NOVEMBER 17TH.
articles.summary: We made an important bet on protecting data 15 years ago. AI just raised the stakes. Meet the Virtru Data Harbor Platform. Control AI agents by controlling the data itself.

articles.title: JOIN US FOR THE LAUNCH EVENT →
GOOGLE CLOUD ADDS SELF-MANAGED VMWARE CLOUD FOUNDATION ON BARE METAL
articles.summary: Google Cloud has launched general availability for a self-managed VMware Cloud Foundation solution on dedicated bare-metal hardware across 22 regions. The new offering gives customers root access across ESXi, vCenter, and NSX, with users driving upgrades and patching using their own portable VCF subscriptions. It complements Google's existing managed VMware Engine, joining similar customer-operated bare-metal options from AWS and Oracle.

articles.title: RED HAT EYES AUTOMATED CLOUD MANAGEMENT GAINS WITH OPENSHIFT 5 RELEASE
articles.summary: Red Hat announced general availability of OpenShift 5, introducing AI-assisted troubleshooting, anomaly detection, and supervised remediation for hybrid cloud operations. The release also adds automated update checks and expanded support for running containers, virtual machines, and AI workloads together, aiming to reduce day-to-day platform management overhead.

articles.title: BROADCOM CONTRIBUTES VM API OPEN SOURCE PROJECT TO CLOUD NATIVE COMPUTING FOUNDATION
articles.summary: Broadcom's VM API project has been accepted into the CNCF Sandbox, introducing a vendor-neutral approach to managing virtual machines through Kubernetes APIs. The company also announced participation in a new workload conformance initiative and more than 20 validated VMware vSphere Kubernetes Service partner solutions. The efforts could improve consistency across mixed virtualization and container environments.

articles.title: HOW CISCO BUILT AN ENTERPRISE AI FACTORY: SCALING ECONOMICS, PERFORMANCE, AND SECURITY
articles.summary: Cisco IT built a multi-tenant AI infrastructure platform combining pooled networking, NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, rack-level cooling, and integrated security. Cisco reports tripling average GPU utilization from 15% to approximately 50% and expanding its GPU footprint sixfold without adding data center space. The architecture is designed to improve infrastructure economics while supporting enterprise AI workloads at scale.

articles.title: I'M THE BOTTLENECK
articles.summary: Managing AI coding agents can increase developer exhaustion through constant context switching, decision fatigue, and pressure to keep agents running. These patterns can lead to cognitive surrender, where developers increasingly defer decisions to AI without fully understanding the results. Rather than optimizing code output, teams should redesign workflows around human attention and recovery.

articles.title: AI SPEND IS INCREASING BUT ISN'T CAUSING A SAASPOCALYPSE
articles.summary: The data indicates that this AI spending growth is not cannibalizing traditional software budgets, as AI-heavy companies actually increased their software spending as well.

articles.title: QUICKLY CONFIRM SYSTEM-APPLIED CLASSIFICATION LABELS IN GOOGLE DRIVE, DOCS, SHEETS, AND SLIDES
articles.summary: Google is simplifying the review of automatically applied file-classification labels with new Accept and Edit buttons.

articles.title: AI HARDWARE STARTUP NOMINAL TRIPLES VALUATION TO $3B IN 8 MONTHS
articles.summary: Nominal raised $240 million in Series C funding at a $3 billion valuation, up from $1 billion in March.
